speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: There are other forms of renewable energy we can consider, such as small unit waste to energy, hydrogen-based genset and wind energy.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: But in this Motion, we will only consider battery and solar for simplicity.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Kindly take note, any proposed design and data used in my speech are primarily from our very own assessment and should the government of the day would like to comment, correct or even share their data, I truly welcome the initiative.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Before I proceed further, I declare my position.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: I am the Executive Chairman of an engineering firm that designs and integrates customised power systems and energy management solutions.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: My company has completed over 3,000 projects across 20 countries.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: I hold an engineering degree and have practised in this field for more than two decades.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: I shall first describe Singapore's current power generation architecture.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Second, I will examine credible disruption scenarios, both historical and future.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Third, I will present a technically grounded, decentralised strategy to counter those disruptions.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: There are seven parts to my speech, and these are very succinct.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: In 2018, a major blackout affected parts of Ang Mo Kio, Yishun and other areas.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Each time, the root cause traced back to a localised fault that propagated because our grid lacks sufficient segmentation and distributed back-up.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: At the building level, many industrial and commercial facilities maintain diesel generator sets to power critical loads.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: But these come with well-known limitations – fuel storage constraints, refuelling logistics during extended outages, emissions, noise and maintenance burdens.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: On a side note, I understand that a micro-grid project has been initiated by the Government in 2018 but till now, we have not seen the outcome of the project nor implementation of the solutions in a bigger scale.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Probably the Ministry-in-charge can update on the development of the micro-grid project in Pulau Ubin.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: The second part, disruption scenarios beyond the conventional.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: A geopolitical event or natural disaster disrupts gas supply.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: We do have back-up supplies, but after that, power plants begin tripping.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: A coordinated cyber attack targets the main power control systems and several power plants' supervisory control and data acquisition networks.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Increasingly intense tropical storms, lightning or flooding events can cause simultaneous faults on multiple transmission lines.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: In all these scenarios, a single centralised solution – building more gas plants or interconnectors – does not solve the fundamental problem.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: I propose a layered, distributed architecture comprising three technical elements.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Element one: rooftop and space-optimised solar building integrated photovoltaics, which has been well implemented by the Government.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: I am glad to see that solar photovoltaics have been deployed on Housing and Development Board (HDB) blocks' rooftops and floating farms on reservoirs.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: We should aim to have deployment on every available suitable surface – multi-storey car parks, school roofs and industrial warehouse roof tops.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Modern solar modules achieve 24% to 25% efficiency.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Pair each solar installation with a lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) BESS.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: LFP chemistry offers superior thermal stability, longer cycle life – 6,000 to 10,000 cycles – and no thermal runaway risk – critical for high-rise residential applications.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: I will give an example of technical sizing, for the sake of presenting my speech.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Take Block 95 at Aljunied Crescent, with an estimated essential load per block, with two lifts, pump and corridor lighting, and a total load of 22 kilowatts.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: To protect the load running for four to eight hours, the required BESS for 22 kilowatts by six hours, assuming we take a safe margin, is 132 kilowatt-hours.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: A 150 kilowatt-hour LFP battery cabinet occupies roughly two square metres and fits in a corner of the existing electrical room or rooftop.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: That is the load profile for the flat itself.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, with solar generation, the battery charges during the day.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: When utility fails, an automatic transfer switch with less than 50 millisecond transition seamlessly hands over to BESS.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Smart power management controllers shed non-essential loads within 200 milliseconds, preserving stored energy for essential functions.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: The deployment of BESS can be done even on an apartment basis.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: In other words, every unit apartment will have a secondary power, which is another set of batteries, to ensure that every unit will run when the power fails.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Like how every unit has a bomb shelter, now each unit has a BESS solution to power the apartment during emergency or power disruption situations.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: This will have a separate calculation for internal use.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Element three: now that you have the solar power and the battery, comes the control system.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: A building energy controller (BEC) monitors real-time state of charge, solar generation and load priority.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: It uses Modbus Transmission Control Protocol or other forms of protocols to communicate with smart breakers and sub-metres.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: The priority levels will look at: Level 1: critical, always powered.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: For lifts, fire systems, water pumps, corridor emergency lighting and security cameras; and Level 2: non-essential, shed immediately on outage.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: For air conditioners, water heaters, non-critical office equipment and electric vehicle (EV) chargers.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Residents would receive an SMS or app notification: "Grid failure detected.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Lifts and water pumps remain operational." Transparency builds trust.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: One HDB block becomes energy-independent for essential loads, but the real leap occurs when we interconnect neighbouring blocks, commercial buildings and industrial facilities into a local microgrid.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: When utility power fails, the controller islanded the constituency from the main grid.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Each block runs on its own battery initially.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: For longer outages beyond four to six hours, the microgrid controller enables peer-to-peer energy sharing.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: A block with surplus battery transfers power to a block running low.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: A commercial building with a large rooftop array shares solar generation with nearby residential blocks.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Similar microgrids operate today in various countries such as the US, Italy, China and many others.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Scale this design to every constituency – Ang Mo Kio, Tampines, Tanjong Pagar, Jurong, Sengkang and beyond.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Each constituency becomes a grid-forming island, capable of operating independently for eight to 24 hours without mainland utility power.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: The total rooftop solar is around 1.5 gigawatt-peak potential across all suitable surfaces.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: This distributed architecture provides what no central plant can – inherent redundancy.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: A failure in one block affects only that block.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: A failure in one constituency does not cascade to another.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Diesel gensets cost approximately $0.40 to $0.60 per kilowatt-hour to operate, plus the cost of maintenance.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: With the current conflict in the Middle East, these prices have soared even higher.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Solar plus BESS, amortised over 15 years, costs $0.15 to $0.25 per kilowatt-hour for back-up power.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: These distributed BESS assets, when not used for back-up, can provide frequency regulation and peak shaving to the main grid.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: It is not only for power back-up, it can also be used for peak shaving.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: EMA could aggregate them as a virtual power plant (VPP), generating revenue that offsets capital costs.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: After a major outage, central plants require hours to resynchronise.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Elderly residents on upper floors are not stranded, nor will they be in the dark.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Every kilowatt-hour of diesel displaced reduces CO2 by approximately 2.7 kilogrammes.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Nationally, this could cut 200,000 tonnes annually, the equivalent of removing 60,000 cars from our roads.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: The last part, part seven, implementation pathway, practical and phased.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Pilot in one constituency – Macpherson or Sengkang.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Deploy solar plus BESS on 30 HDB blocks, integrate with microgrid controller and run parallel to the grid for one year.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Collect real-world performance, load data and resident feedback.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Refine smart loading algorithms, integrate with main grid control room and establish VPP (Virtual Power Plant) dispatch protocols.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Every HDB block, every major commercial building, every industrial facility.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Mandate new buildings to include solar-ready roofs and BESS-ready electrical rooms.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Even though we have somewhat approximate figures for the capital cost for the above, but it is best we compute thoroughly.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: I believe the ability to ensure the reliability of power for all residents during grid failure is immeasurable.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: But our energy architecture remains a 20th century central model in a 21st century risk environment.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: We cannot rely solely on imported gas, central plants and diesel generators that fail when we need them most.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: I offer my engineering experience to that effort without reservation.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: Let us not wait for the next blackout to remind us what resilience means.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The power grid is like the backbone of our body.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It holds the system together, connecting power generation sources and end-consumers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Government recognises the importance of having a resilient and reliable grid to power our economy and our daily lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: A key factor underpinning our grid's resilience is its interconnectedness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The grid is connected to all our power stations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: If any generating unit were to trip, other generating units can ramp up to meet the shortfall.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The transmission and distribution network itself is also designed with some redundancy to minimise the impact in the event of any single equipment failure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We recognise that a centralised grid also means that upstream disruptions such as interruptions to fuel supply may have system-wide consequences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: That is why we have diversified our sources of gas supplies and maintain fuel reserves in case of disruptions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As we introduce more distributed energy resources and renewables such as solar, the grid design will become even more important.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: On the supply side, our energy mix will become more diverse as we scale up domestic solar and electricity imports.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will have more distributed energy resources across the island such as rooftop solar panels and battery energy storage systems.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Specifically for solar, power generation fluctuates with cloud cover and weather in the daytime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The intermittency brings new challenges to the system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: On the demand side, Singapore's electricity demand is expected to increase significantly with the growth of electricity-intensive loads such as data centres and electric vehicles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: There will be a greater impetus to manage load profiles to optimise usage of grid capacity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We therefore need to accelerate grid innovation to build a more responsive grid while ensuring system stability and optimising land use.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: First, we are planning ahead and putting the required infrastructure in place to support the grid of the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is essentially the research and development arm that will help keep Singapore's grid ahead of the curve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Beyond planning, we are also deploying new physical assets to make the grid more resilient.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Sembcorp's large-scale battery energy storage system on Jurong Island is one example.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It can respond quickly to sudden shifts in supply, helping to keep the system stable when renewable energy sources like solar fluctuate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Second, we are making the grid more flexible and responsive to change.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: With more solar, batteries and electric vehicles coming online, the grid needs to be able to handle greater variability in both supply and demand.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Flexibility is what allows the grid to absorb those fluctuations without compromising stability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Essentially, EV charging stations and smaller battery storage systems can participate in helping to stabilise the grid.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For instance, by drawing less power or releasing stored energy when the system is under stress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: EMA is currently piloting this with ComfortDelGro to test how it works in a real-world setting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: EMA will also launch a Virtual Power Plant pilot.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Virtual Power Plants are digital platforms that can aggregate and optimise distributed energy resources such as solar and batteries as a single power source to meet demand.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Azhar raised the idea of deploying off-grid and micro-grid power systems across Singapore to support grid resilience and also to serve as backup power in the event of potential disruptions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Indeed, microgrids are one of several distributed energy solutions that we will study further.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: If managed well, such distributed energy solutions have the potential to provide an additional layer of safeguard by providing energy, ancillary services, or demand response to smoothen peak periods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: However, their suitability depends on the operating environment and specific needs, provided the safety requirements and technical standards are met.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Azhar suggested the possibility of deploying battery energy storage systems in HDB blocks and microgrids in every town.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will have to study this further, because high power battery systems also have to comply with the Singapore Civil Defence Force's fire safety standards, which could require additional space and safety infrastructure in densely populated HDB blocks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: They could cost more to operate than larger grid systems and may offer lower power reliability if they lack sufficient reserves and redundancies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As technology matures and deployment models evolve, we expect many of these challenges to become more manageable over time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Today, microgrids are deployed in Singapore, primarily to support test-bedding of new technologies and in places where there are specific needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Singapore Institute of Technology has collaborated with SP Group to develop Singapore’s first experimental urban micro-grid on campus.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The micro-grid will support test-bedding of new technologies and solutions in a controlled environment, while providing students the opportunity to work with industry partners and energy startups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In addition, decentralised off-grid energy solutions are commonly deployed by commercial and industrial users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Facilities with critical loads, such as data centres, may invest in on-site generation, battery storage or hybrid systems to enhance reliability, based on their specific needs and constraints.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Diesel generators are an off-grid solution that is being used today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: They are typically deployed as localised back-up for individual facilities, such as hospitals and data centres, to continue running their essential operations in the event of power disruption.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: A battery energy storage system is an alternative source of back-up power, although the upfront cost of deploying battery energy storage system is currently still higher than for diesel generators at the same power setting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: A battery energy storage system also needs to be recharged, unlike diesel generators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As batteries become more cost-competitive, we expect more end-users to deploy batteries as off-grid solutions, if it meets their operational requirements and as a way of lowering their emissions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Azhar asked about the Pulau Ubin Micro Grid.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will continue to study how micro-grids and other distributed energy resources can complement our existing measures to support Singapore's energy resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As we do so, we welcome partnerships with the industry on innovative new solutions that can be applied in Singapore, be it on micro-grids or other aspects of grid planning, development, and operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Last year, EMA launched the Energy Grid 3.0 Grant Call.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Research consortia were invited to submit proposals aimed at enhancing grid planning and operations capabilities, as well as solutions to manage new needs such as inertia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These efforts reflect our commitment to building a resilient and innovative grid, and we look forward to more impactful and transformative partnerships with industry on this front.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will continue to invest in grid innovation, study developments from around the world, and work closely with industry and researchers to deploy suitable, cost-effective solutions for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Together, we will build a strong backbone that powers Singapore's future.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We just have a few more minutes before time.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman
text: I just want to thank Minister of State Gan for the sharing about the strategy.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman
text: Just a couple of comments, if I can.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman
text: Having said that, on a final point, the micro-grid itself is just another, I would call it a, if you look at the highway, it is just another road, path, for every commuter to use as well.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: In fact, data centres are also actively looking for alternative solutions that are more sustainable.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: That will give some alternative to the data centres.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 11.00 am.
